title: Federal Judge Orders Release of Houston ICE Shooting Witness Held in Detention
excerpt: A federal judge ordered DHS to release Jose Trinidad Rojas Pliego, a witness to the fatal ICE shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo who had been held in immigration detention, within 48 hours. Advocates alleged his detention was intended to suppress his testimony.
content:
On July 26, 2026, a federal judge ordered the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to release Jose Trinidad Rojas Pliego—one of three passengers in Lorenzo Salgado Araujo's work van during the July 7 Houston ICE shooting—within 48 hours.

Rojas Pliego and two other witnesses had filed habeas corpus petitions arguing their continued detention in immigration custody was unconstitutional and appeared designed to suppress testimony contradicting the government's account of the shooting. All three men had been taken to the Montgomery ICE Processing Center in Conroe, Texas, after the shooting.

  • The Texas Tribune reported that Rojas Pliego left the Montgomery Processing Center on Wednesday, July 29, within the court's 48-hour window.
  • The two remaining witnesses—Daniel Tirado Pantoja and the victim's brother Victor Hugo Salgado Araujo—filed similar petitions but had not yet received court orders at the time of initial reporting.
  • ICE had not publicly identified the agent who fired the shot more than two weeks after the killing.
